title: Mrs. Ilana Alouf: "Parashat Lekh Lekha"

chapters.title: The command of Lech Lecha
chapters.about: Avraham's initiation of the relationship with Hashem and the command to leave his past.

chapters.title: Leaving the past
chapters.about: The necessity of deleting old habits and identity to build a new nation.

chapters.title: Avraham and Terach
chapters.about: The timeline of Avraham's departure and the importance of first impressions.

chapters.title: Revelation and the 10 tests
chapters.about: The nature of prophecy for Avraham compared to Moshe Rabbenu.

chapters.title: The 2,000 years of Torah
chapters.about: The historical division of the 6,000 years and Avraham's role.

chapters.title: The meaning of ve'nivrechu
chapters.about: Analyzing the word ve'nivrechu and the concept of grafting families.

chapters.title: Exile and humility
chapters.about: Avraham's choice of exile and the importance of humility in connecting to Hashem.

summary: Mrs. Alouf discusses the command of Lech Lecha to Avraham Avinu as a transformative process of leaving his past to build a new identity and nation. She explores the concept of the 2,000 years of Torah beginning with Avraham and explains how Am Yisrael serves as a model for global unity among families. The class also examines the spiritual significance of the 70 sacrifices brought during Sukkot as a way to bring blessings to all nations.
questions: Why did Hashem command Avraham to leave his land, birthplace, and father's house?
What is the significance of the 2,000 years of Torah starting with Avraham?
How does the concept of 'mishpachot' (families) relate to the goal of world peace?
Why did Avraham choose exile as the form of punishment for his descendants?
What is the connection between the 70 sacrifices of Sukkot and the nations of the world?
